validation.notes: Repair: recoverToolInvocation in packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts replayed a durable effect whenever only the persisted call intent said "safe" (!cancelled && call.replay === "safe"), ignoring the current tool declaration. It now replays only when the persisted intent and the currently declared tool are both "safe" (&& tool !== undefined && tool.replay === "safe"); a missing or downgraded declaration falls through to the existing interrupted path, which reads the durable checkpoint and publishes an interrupted, isError tool result instead of throwing or executing the effect. Validated with the required standalone Node 24 VM regression (.prale-eval/regression.mjs) that drives the real recoverToolInvocation/interruptedOutcome through the read-only .prale-eval/subject.mjs boundary fakes (only checkpoint IO, effect execution and outcome publication are faked). It asserts 64 cross-realm-normalized invariants over 6 scenarios: missing tool declaration (persisted safe, tool absent) settles as interrupted with events [read, publish], no checkpoint clear, no invocation and no replayed effect result; changed declaration safe->never interrupts; current declaration without a replay policy interrupts; persisted never + current safe interrupts; cancelled call interrupts even when both are safe; and the jointly safe, non-cancelled call still replays exactly once with events [clear, invoke, effect-complete, publish] and its real non-error result. Interrupted outcomes are also asserted to preserve the durable checkpoint content/details and to carry the 'external outcome is unknown' marker, toolCallId and terminate=false. Negative control: restoring the original faulty condition made the regression fail with AssertionError 'missing tool declaration: recovery must read the durable checkpoint and settle without clearing/replaying the effect, got [clear, invoke, effect-complete, publish]' (exit 1); after restoring the fix the script exits 0 again. Limitation: the repository's own vitest/tsc validation could not be run because no node_modules are present in this workspace and installing dependencies is out of scope, so the Node 24 VM regression against the real production source is the focused validation used.
